title: Writing: A Film or Book Review

writingModel.placeholder: Introduce the work: title, director/author, genre, brief context
writingModel.hint: One or two sentences — place the work in context without plot summary

writingModel.placeholder: What does the work attempt to do? What is its central concern or approach?
writingModel.hint: Not a plot summary — describe its artistic ambition and methods

writingModel.placeholder: Analyse two or three specific elements: language, structure, cinematography, character, theme
writingModel.hint: Use cause/effect and purpose linkers: "in order to…", "as a result…"

writingModel.placeholder: What are its strengths and weaknesses? Does it achieve what it set out to do?
Final balanced judgement: who should watch/read it and why?
writingModel.hint: Use "on balance," "overall," "ultimately" for a strong conclusion

writingTemplate.hint: Name the work and categorise it
writingTemplate.placeholder: The film / novel / explores / examines / challenges

writingTemplate.prefix: What sets it apart from conventional
writingTemplate.placeholder: films/novels of its genre / ambiguous structure / refusal to resolve its central conflict

writingTemplate.hint: Analyse one specific technique and its purpose
writingTemplate.placeholder: fragmented time / symbolism / contrast between light and dark / disorient the viewer and mirror the protagonist's mental state
the pacing is slow in places / powerfully unsettling and ultimately rewarding
despite its demands on the audience, this is a work of genuine artistic importance that rewards careful attention

items: The film/novel explores the theme of… through the lens of…
What distinguishes this work is its refusal to…
The director/author employs a fragmented structure in order to…
Central to the work is the tension between… and…
The narrative is driven not by plot but by…
The use of [technique] creates/produces/achieves…
Due to the director's choice to…, the viewer/reader…
The recurring motif of… serves to…
In contrast to conventional [genre], this work…
The [lighting/score/sentence structure] is used so as to avoid…
Although [weakness], the overall achievement is…
Despite occasional [weakness], the work succeeds in…
Its greatest strength is… ; however, it falls short in…
The film/novel is not without its flaws — nevertheless, it…
On balance, the strengths outweigh the weaknesses because…
On balance, this is a work that…
Overall, despite its demands, this is…
Ultimately, the film/novel succeeds because it…
In conclusion, I would recommend this to readers who…
This is not a work for everyone; however, those willing to engage with it will find…

questions.text: "___ its slow pace, the film is deeply engaging throughout." (concession)
"The director uses extreme close-ups ___ create an uncomfortable sense of intimacy." (purpose)
questions.correct: in order to / so as to
questions.hint: "In order to / so as to + infinitive" = artistic intention

questions.text: "The novel's ending is ambiguous. ___, critics have reached very different conclusions." (effect)
"___ the film's commercial failure, it has since become a critical landmark." (unexpected positive — concession)
"___, this novel is one of the most significant literary achievements of the decade." (formal conclusion)
"On balance" is used to introduce a final, balanced judgement in a review.
questions.hint: "On balance" = weighing all considerations before a final verdict

questions.text: "The author withholds the protagonist's name ___ the reader shares their sense of anonymity." (purpose: reader is the subject)
questions.hint: "So that + subject + verb" = purpose with a new subject

questions.text: "___ being critically acclaimed, it won no commercial awards." (concession + gerund)
